T318 reconciled the retirement count, which had been reported three different ways. Re-measured against the ground truth (the §1 table itself), all four sources agree at 116. The reconciliation, with the command beside each figure, is written into register-tree-map.md §3.1. Summary of which was wrong and why: (1) the '117' figure was a measurement artifact — the unscoped `grep -c '^\|.*RETIRED'` (BSD grep, literal pipe) matched 116 §1 table cells plus one §3 prose row (line 538, '...+ 116 RETIRED'); scoped to §1 the table has 116. The §1 table content was always 116; nothing in it needed changing. (2) the '118' figure lived only in the `notes` prose string of findings/T305-tree-map.json; the structured `tree_map` object in that same file has exactly 116 RETIRED entries. The 118 was a prose typo with no structural backing; T318 corrected the notes string to 116 (correction noted in that field). (3) the §2 header (116) and the six §2.x family subtotals (21+45+24+9+14+3=116) were correct as written. The whole-file `grep -c RETIRED` over-counts (it was 119 = 116 cells + 3 prose before T318 added §3.1; it is higher now because §3.1 itself mentions RETIRED in prose) and is NOT the table-cell count — the robust cell count is the §1-scoped command = 116. No row's mapping or retirement proposal was altered to make the arithmetic work.

Deliverable two: docs/epic-01-markovian/retirement-ruling-sheet.md — one line per proposed retirement (116 rows, grouped by the six families), each carrying the claim ID, current register status, family reason (one line), a 'what is lost if retired' column (mechanically cross-checked: in-register live dependents parsed from the register dependents column with edge kind read from the live row's depends-on; external docs/ citations grepped across docs/**/*.md excluding CLAIMS.md / register-tree-map.md / the sheet), and an empty RULING column. Sheet row count = 116 = the reconciled retirement count. 27 of 116 rows have >=1 live in-register dependent. 8 rows are flagged ⚑ sole-`e:`(evidenced-by)-evidence for a live still-believed (not FALSE-AS-SCOPED) row: 3x3.ANCHOR, 4x3.M3, 4x4.ANCHOR, 4x4.M4, 4x4.M6, 4x4.PARALLEL, CODE.UNDEF, GLOBAL.FIN-BRACKET. Per the T318 bar these are not retirement candidates until the live row's depends-on is re-pointed.

The three-to-four rows I would most contest (where T305's retirement proposal is wrong or premature):

1. 4x4.M6 (old-artifact family, MEASUREMENT). It is the `e:` (evidenced-by) source for TWO live, still-believed, Z-TABLE-FAITHFUL finisher-soundness rows: 4x4.F2 (UNTESTED, depends_on `e:4x4.M6`) and 4x4.F3 (UNTESTED, depends_on `e:4x4.M6`). For 4x4.F3 it is the sole `e:` source. These are the 4x4 finisher-soundness claims the project still owes — retiring the measurement they rest on leaves both with a dangling evidence edge. This is the textbook 'sole evidence for something still believed' the brief warns against.

2. CODE.UNDEF (player family, PROVEN) together with 4x4.PARALLEL (old-artifact family, MEASUREMENT). 4x4.B43 (live, Z-NONCLAIMS, the NC4 '3.4% clean leak with UNDEF guard' measurement) has exactly two `e:` sources — `e:CODE.UNDEF` and `e:4x4.PARALLEL` — and BOTH are proposed for retirement in this same sheet. Retiring both retires 4x4.B43's entire evidence base at once. Separately, CODE.UNDEF is arguably mis-family: it is the UNDEF sentinel convention the leak instrument runs under, not a player-side claim; the family label 'player' (reason §2.3) does not fit a PROVEN sentinel a live NC4 measurement depends on.

3. 4x3.M3 (old-artifact family, MEASUREMENT). It is the SOLE `e:` evidence for 4x4.D3 (UNTESTED, Z-TABLE-FAITHFUL, 'writes-off 4x4 tractability — feasibility of the faithful generation'). 4x4.D3 is the feasibility argument for the faithful 4x4 generation the whole Track A effort is built on, and it extrapolates from 4x3.M3's writes-on solve cost. Retiring 4x3.M3 removes 4x4.D3's only evidence while 4x4.D3 is still UNTESTED and load-bearing (4x4.F2, 4x4.F3, 4x4.F4, GLOBAL.H4a, GLOBAL.H1-CENSUS all depend on 4x4.D3).

4. GLOBAL.FIN-BRACKET (design family, MEASUREMENT). It is the `e:` evidence recorded by GLOBAL.H5c (PROVEN (as an implication), Z-NONCLAIMS) — and GLOBAL.H5c is the load-bearing 'edge that orphans the finisher' (§4-O1). Retiring the evidence a PROVEN-as-implication load-bearing row depends on is premature; the edge should be re-pointed or the implication re-justified before the row is retired.

A sheet that agrees with everything is not a review; these four are where I think T305's proposal is wrong. The other 112 proposals are, on the mechanical cross-check, clean or only-historically-cited retirements that the human can rule on the family reason alone.

What I checked vs judged: the in-register live-dependents and edge-kind data are mechanical (parsed from CLAIMS.md columns, no judgment). The 'sole evidence for something still believed' flag is judged from that mechanical data plus the live row's status (PROVEN/CLAIMED/UNTESTED/MEASUREMENT = still believed; FALSE-AS-SCOPED = not). The 'most contest' selection is judged, not mechanical — it weighs how many live rows lose their evidence, whether the live row is still believed, and whether the live row is load-bearing (cited by a tree node). I did NOT re-argue any family's retirement reason; the family reason in the sheet is copied verbatim in spirit from register-tree-map.md §2.

What I could not establish: whether any live row that cites a retiring row as `e:` has INDEPENDENT evidence I did not surface — the register's depends_on lists all `e:` sources, so for the flagged rows I report the full set, but whether the row's prose claim could stand on its other listed evidence is a judgment for the human at ruling time. I did not run zig build test (this row writes no engine/buildable code); claimlint was run and passes (C9=0, calibration PASS, 323 rows).
